summary: Erik and Martin Demaine's mathematical 'Tetris Font': an unstyled academic page whose whole first screen is a renderer. Typed text is drawn as SVG letters built from exactly one of each Tetris piece, animated as pieces dropping and rotating into place, with puzzle and dissection modes and GIF/SVG export; explanatory paragraphs on the design and the related complexity results follow.

instances.look: Plain HTML table header: 'Tetris Font' as a blue underlined h1 link at left, 'by Erik Demaine and Martin Demaine, 2020 & 2026' as an h2 at right, browser-default Times

A row of default HTML form controls (textarea 'Enter text to render', checkboxes, a Speed range, a Font select) above a wide white stage where coloured Tetris pieces with black outlines fall onto a grey floor bar and stack into the letters of the typed text
instances.ux: Type in the textarea and the SVG re-renders; Animate replays the drop sequence (Include rotations, Speed 0–10); toggles for Puzzle font (pieces placed at drop height so you decode the letter), Black pieces (dissection puzzle), Grid, Rotation center, Bottom floor; Font select picks the 7-piece font or a one-piece-type font (I light/bold, J, L, S, T, Z); below the stage: GIF width field, Download Animated GIF, Download SVG and 'Hide all but font rendering' (not cut as a block, attached here); 'Obscure in URL' rot13s the text in the shareable query string
instances.learn: When the font is a system of parts, render the text by assembling it from those parts in time: the animation explains the construction rule better than any diagram, and an export button turns it into a toy

reconstruction.layout: Full-width 3-cell table of controls (~110px tall): textarea 4×40 with label at left, Animate group in the middle, Font select and display toggles at right; output div 100% wide × ~676px with the rendered SVG letters sitting on a grey floor bar ~520px down; download row right-aligned underneath
reconstruction.typography: UI in browser defaults (16px Times New Roman labels, monospace textarea); the 'font' itself is not a webfont but SVG polygons on a unit grid, each letter ~7 cells wide, rendered ~40px per cell at 1440
reconstruction.behaviour: SVG.js builds each glyph from piece polygons (classes .I .O .S .Z .T .L .J with Tetris standard fills, 0.2 black stroke, round joins); with Animate on, pieces spawn above the letter and fall cell by cell (optionally rotating per the Super Rotation System) in their drop order; root classes (anim-true, rotate-true, puzzle-false, black-false, grid-false, floor-true) switch the display modes; furls syncs every control to the URL; GIF export renders frames at the chosen width
reconstruction.content: Default text 'text'; inline codes [7] [I] [I2] [J] [L] [S] [T] [Z] switch fonts mid-text
reconstruction.assets: Piece geometry per glyph (fonts.js, pieces.js); no images
reconstruction.html: table#data > textarea#text + input#rot | input#anim, #rotate, input#speed[type=range][min=0][max=10], #puzzle, #black | select#font, #grid, #center, #floor, #hud; div#output > svg; div.noprint > input#width + button#downloadGIF + button#downloadSVG + button#nohud
